subject: business-studies
title: PESTLE Analysis
welcome_lead: Scan six external forces shaping every business decision.
meta_desc: A-Level External Environment: PESTLE analysis framework.
final_note: External change is constant - PESTLE keeps the radar tuned.

concepts.def: Growth, inflation, interest rates, exchange rates.
Employment law, consumer protection, competition law.

walkthroughs.body_html: PESTLE forces managers to look outside the firm. It surfaces threats and opportunities that internal SWOT can miss - Brexit, AI and net zero are all PESTLE drivers.
Brainstorm under each heading, then score each issue for likelihood and impact. Focus on the top 3 to 5 - a 60-bullet PESTLE that triggers no action is useless.
Letters interact: a technological change like remote work has social, economic and legal knock-ons. Treat PESTLE as a system, not a checklist.

mcqs.q: Rising interest rates fall under which PESTLE letter?
New data protection law (GDPR) is primarily which letter?
Can a business control its external environment?
options: Economic growth above 5% a year is illegal.
Well-run businesses can simply decide to remove external threats.
Largely no — PESTLE factors like interest rates, law and demographics lie outside its control, but a firm can anticipate them, lobby, and adapt its strategy.
Businesses vote each year to set national interest rates.

mcqs.q: Do rising interest rates affect only firms with loans?
options: Businesses vote each year to set national interest rates.
If a business has no borrowing, interest rates are irrelevant to it.
Interest rates only apply to savings accounts.
No — they also cut consumer spending on credit-bought goods, influence exchange rates and change investment plans, hitting demand even for debt-free firms.

mcqs.q: Is a growing economy good news for every business?
options: Economic growth above 5% a year is illegal.
Mostly but not all — sellers of inferior goods and discount retailers can lose customers as incomes rise, and booms bring higher wages, costs and interest rates.
Economic growth benefits all businesses equally.
Businesses vote each year to set national interest rates.
